questions.de: In Deutschland dürfen Menschen offen etwas gegen die Regierung sagen, weil …
questions.en: In Germany, people are allowed to openly say something against the government because …

opts.en: people have the right to vote.

questions.exp_de: In Deutschland gilt Meinungsfreiheit (Art. 5 GG) — Menschen dürfen offen Kritik an der Regierung äußern.
questions.exp_en: Freedom of speech (Meinungsfreiheit) is one of the most important fundamental rights guaranteed by Article 5 of the German Basic Law (Grundgesetz). It means every person in Germany has the right to freely express their opinions in speech, writing, and images — including criticism of the government. This right is essential to a functioning democracy.

questions.de: In Deutschland können Eltern bis zum 14. Lebensjahr ihres Kindes entscheiden, ob es in der Schule am …
questions.en: In Germany, parents can decide until their child's 14th year of life whether it participates in … at school.
questions.exp_de: Eltern können bis zum 14. Lebensjahr ihres Kindes entscheiden, ob es am Religionsunterricht teilnimmt; danach entscheidet das Kind selbst.
questions.exp_en: Under German law, parents have the right to decide whether their child participates in religious education at school until the child turns 14. After age 14, the child can decide for themselves whether to attend religious classes (this is called "Religionsmündigkeit" — religious maturity). All other school subjects like history, politics, and languages are mandatory.

questions.de: Deutschland ist ein Rechtsstaat. Was ist damit gemeint?
questions.en: Germany is a constitutional state (Rechtsstaat). What does this mean?

opts.de: Alle Einwohnerinnen/Einwohner und der Staat müssen sich an die Gesetze halten.
opts.en: All residents and the state must abide by the laws.

opts.de: Der Staat muss sich nicht an die Gesetze halten.
opts.en: The state does not have to abide by the laws.

opts.de: Nur Deutsche müssen die Gesetze befolgen.
opts.en: Only Germans must obey the laws.

questions.exp_de: Ein Rechtsstaat bedeutet, dass sowohl die Bürgerinnen und Bürger als auch der Staat selbst an geltende Gesetze gebunden sind.
questions.exp_en: The term "Rechtsstaat" (rule of law / constitutional state) means that the government itself is bound by the law — it cannot act arbitrarily. Everyone, including the state and all its institutions, must follow the law. This principle is a cornerstone of German democracy and is established in the Basic Law.

questions.de: Welches Recht gehört zu den Grundrechten in Deutschland?
questions.en: Which right is one of the fundamental rights in Germany?
questions.exp_de: Die Meinungsfreiheit ist eines der in Deutschland garantierten Grundrechte.
questions.exp_en: Freedom of expression (Meinungsfreiheit) is a fundamental right protected by Article 5 of the Basic Law. The other options — the right to bear arms, vigilantism (literally "fist law"), and self-help justice — are not fundamental rights in Germany. In fact, vigilantism and self-help justice are illegal. Germany does not have a constitutional right to bear arms like the United States.

questions.de: Wahlen in Deutschland sind frei. Was bedeutet das?
questions.en: Elections in Germany are free. What does this mean?

opts.de: Man darf Geld annehmen, wenn man dafür eine bestimmte Kandidatin/einen bestimmten Kandidaten wählt.
opts.en: You are allowed to accept money if you vote for a specific candidate.

opts.de: Nur Personen, die noch nie im Gefängnis waren, dürfen wählen.
opts.en: Only people who have never been in prison are allowed to vote.

opts.de: Die Wählerin/der Wähler darf bei der Wahl weder beeinflusst noch zu einer bestimmten Stimmabgabe gezwungen werden und keine Nachteile durch die Wahl haben.
opts.en: Voters must not be influenced or forced to vote in a certain way, nor suffer any disadvantages as a result of their vote.

questions.exp_de: Freie Wahlen bedeuten, dass niemand beim Wählen beeinflusst, gezwungen oder benachteiligt werden darf.
questions.exp_en: German elections follow five principles: they are universal, direct, free, equal, and secret (allgemein, unmittelbar, frei, gleich, geheim). "Free" means voters cannot be pressured, bribed, or forced to vote in any particular way. There is no compulsory voting in Germany — voting is a right, not an obligation. Accepting money for votes is illegal.

questions.de: Wie heißt die deutsche Verfassung?
questions.en: What is the name of the German constitution?
questions.exp_de: Die deutsche Verfassung heißt Grundgesetz.
questions.exp_en: The German constitution is called the "Grundgesetz" (Basic Law). It was adopted on May 23, 1949 and was originally intended as a temporary constitution for West Germany until reunification. After reunification in 1990, it became the constitution for all of Germany. It was deliberately not called "Verfassung" (constitution) to emphasize its provisional nature, but today it functions fully as Germany's constitution.

questions.de: Welches Recht gehört zu den Grundrechten, die nach der deutschen Verfassung garantiert werden? Das Recht auf …
questions.en: Which right is among the fundamental rights guaranteed by the German constitution? The right to …
questions.exp_de: Die Glaubens- und Gewissensfreiheit ist ein durch das Grundgesetz garantiertes Grundrecht.
questions.exp_en: Freedom of faith and conscience (Article 4 of the Basic Law) is a fundamental right in Germany. While the right to work and housing are important societal goals, they are not guaranteed as fundamental rights in the Basic Law. The right to entertainment is not a constitutional right at all.

questions.de: Was steht nicht im Grundgesetz von Deutschland?
questions.en: What is NOT in the German Basic Law?

opts.de: Die Würde des Menschen ist unantastbar.
Alle sollen gleich viel Geld haben.
opts.en: Everyone should have the same amount of money.

opts.de: Jeder Mensch darf seine Meinung sagen.
opts.en: Every person is allowed to express their opinion.

opts.de: Alle sind vor dem Gesetz gleich.
opts.en: All are equal before the law.

questions.exp_de: Das Grundgesetz garantiert die Würde des Menschen, Meinungsfreiheit und Gleichheit vor dem Gesetz — nicht aber materielle Gleichheit ('gleich viel Geld').
questions.exp_en: The Basic Law guarantees human dignity (Article 1), freedom of expression (Article 5), and equality before the law (Article 3). However, it does NOT guarantee that everyone should have the same amount of money. Germany has a social market economy which allows for economic differences while providing a social safety net.

questions.de: Welches Grundrecht gilt in Deutschland nur für Ausländerinnen/Ausländer? Das Grundrecht auf …
questions.en: Which fundamental right in Germany applies only to foreigners? The fundamental right to …
questions.exp_de: Das Asylrecht ist ein Grundrecht, das in Deutschland ausschließlich für Ausländerinnen und Ausländer gilt.
questions.exp_en: The right to asylum (Article 16a of the Basic Law) is the only fundamental right that applies exclusively to foreigners. It gives politically persecuted people the right to seek protection in Germany. All other listed rights — family protection, human dignity, and freedom of opinion — apply to all people in Germany, regardless of nationality.

questions.de: Was ist mit dem deutschen Grundgesetz vereinbar?
questions.en: What is compatible with the German Basic Law?
questions.exp_de: Eine Geldstrafe ist mit dem Grundgesetz vereinbar — Prügelstrafe, Folter und die Todesstrafe sind verboten.
questions.exp_en: Among the listed options, only fines (Geldstrafe) are compatible with the Basic Law. Corporal punishment, torture, and the death penalty are all prohibited. Article 102 explicitly states: "The death penalty is abolished." Article 1 (human dignity) and Article 104 prohibit torture and physical punishment by the state.

questions.de: Wie wird die Verfassung der Bundesrepublik Deutschland genannt?
questions.en: What is the constitution of the Federal Republic of Germany called?
questions.exp_de: Die Verfassung der Bundesrepublik Deutschland wird Grundgesetz genannt.
questions.exp_en: This question is similar to Question 6. The German constitution is called the "Grundgesetz" (Basic Law). It was enacted in 1949 and serves as the supreme law of Germany. All other laws must comply with the Basic Law, and the Federal Constitutional Court (Bundesverfassungsgericht) ensures this.

questions.de: Eine Partei im Deutschen Bundestag will die Pressefreiheit abschaffen. Ist das möglich?
questions.en: A party in the German Bundestag wants to abolish press freedom. Is that possible?

opts.de: Ja, wenn mehr als die Hälfte der Abgeordneten im Bundestag dafür sind.
opts.en: Yes, if more than half of the members of the Bundestag are in favor.

opts.de: Ja, aber dazu müssen zwei Drittel der Abgeordneten im Bundestag dafür sein.
opts.en: Yes, but two-thirds of the members of the Bundestag must be in favor.

opts.de: Nein, denn die Pressefreiheit ist ein Grundrecht. Sie kann nicht abgeschafft werden.
opts.en: No, because press freedom is a fundamental right. It cannot be abolished.

opts.de: Nein, denn nur der Bundesrat kann die Pressefreiheit abschaffen.
opts.en: No, because only the Bundesrat can abolish press freedom.

questions.exp_de: Die Pressefreiheit ist ein unveräußerliches Grundrecht und kann nicht abgeschafft werden, auch nicht durch eine Mehrheit im Bundestag.
questions.exp_en: Press freedom is guaranteed by Article 5 of the Basic Law and is protected by the "eternity clause" (Ewigkeitsklausel, Article 79 Paragraph 3). This clause means that certain core principles of the Basic Law — including fundamental rights like press freedom — can never be abolished or changed, not even with a unanimous vote in parliament.

questions.de: Im Parlament steht der Begriff "Opposition" für …
questions.en: In parliament, the term "opposition" refers to …

opts.de: die Fraktion mit den meisten Abgeordneten.
opts.en: the parliamentary group with the most members.

opts.de: alle Parteien, die bei der letzten Wahl die 5%-Hürde erreichen konnten.
opts.en: all parties that cleared the 5% threshold in the last election.

opts.de: alle Abgeordneten, die nicht zu der Regierungspartei/den Regierungsparteien gehören.
opts.en: all members of parliament who do not belong to the governing party/parties.

questions.exp_de: Im Parlament bezeichnet 'Opposition' alle Abgeordneten, die nicht zur Regierungspartei bzw. den Regierungsparteien gehören.
questions.exp_en: The opposition consists of all parties and their members in parliament who are not part of the government coalition. The opposition plays a crucial role in German democracy: it monitors the government, proposes alternatives, and holds the ruling parties accountable. A strong opposition is considered essential for a healthy democracy.

questions.de: Meinungsfreiheit in Deutschland heißt, dass ich …
questions.en: Freedom of speech in Germany means that I …

opts.de: Passanten auf der Straße beschimpfen darf.
opts.en: am allowed to insult passersby on the street.

opts.de: meine Meinung im Internet äußern kann.
opts.en: can express my opinion on the internet.

opts.de: Nazi-, Hamas- oder Islamischer Staat-Symbole öffentlich tragen darf.
opts.en: am allowed to publicly display Nazi, Hamas, or Islamic State symbols.

opts.de: meine Meinung nur dann äußern darf, solange ich der Regierung nicht widerspreche.
opts.en: may only express my opinion as long as I do not contradict the government.

questions.exp_de: Meinungsfreiheit erlaubt es, die eigene Meinung frei zu äußern — verboten sind aber z. B. das öffentliche Zeigen verfassungsfeindlicher Symbole.
questions.exp_en: Freedom of speech means you can express your opinions freely, including on the internet and even against the government. However, this right has limits: you cannot insult individuals (that is a criminal offense called "Beleidigung"), and displaying symbols of banned organizations like the Nazis, Hamas, or ISIS is illegal in Germany. Note that this question was updated to include Hamas and Islamic State references in recent catalog versions.

questions.de: Was verbietet das deutsche Grundgesetz?
questions.en: What does the German Basic Law prohibit?
questions.exp_de: Das deutsche Grundgesetz verbietet Zwangsarbeit.
questions.exp_en: The Basic Law explicitly prohibits forced labor (Zwangsarbeit) in Article 12. Military service, free choice of profession, and working abroad are all permitted. In fact, free choice of profession is itself a fundamental right (Article 12). Germany historically experienced forced labor during the Nazi era, which is why this prohibition is explicitly stated.

questions.de: Wann ist die Meinungsfreiheit in Deutschland eingeschränkt?
questions.en: When is freedom of speech restricted in Germany?

opts.de: bei der öffentlichen Verbreitung falscher Behauptungen über einzelne Personen
opts.en: when making false public statements about individuals
when expressing opinions about the federal government

questions.exp_de: Die Meinungsfreiheit ist eingeschränkt, wenn falsche Tatsachenbehauptungen über konkrete Personen öffentlich verbreitet werden.
questions.exp_en: While freedom of speech is a fundamental right, it has limits. Spreading false claims about specific individuals (defamation/slander) can be a criminal offense. However, criticizing the government, discussing religions, or criticizing the state are all protected by freedom of speech. The balance between free speech and personal rights is an important principle in German law.

questions.de: Die deutschen Gesetze verbieten …
questions.en: German laws prohibit …

opts.de: Ungleichbehandlung der Bürgerinnen und Bürger durch den Staat.
opts.en: Unequal treatment of citizens by the state.

questions.exp_de: Die deutschen Gesetze verbieten die Ungleichbehandlung von Bürgerinnen und Bürgern durch den Staat.
questions.exp_en: German law prohibits the state from treating citizens unequally (discrimination). This is established in Article 3 of the Basic Law: "All persons are equal before the law." Freedom of opinion, the right to petition, and freedom of assembly are all protected rights — they are NOT prohibited.

questions.de: Welches Grundrecht ist in Artikel 1 des Grundgesetzes der Bundesrepublik Deutschland garantiert?
questions.en: Which fundamental right is guaranteed in Article 1 of the Basic Law?
questions.exp_de: Artikel 1 des Grundgesetzes garantiert die Unantastbarkeit der Menschenwürde.
questions.exp_en: Article 1 of the Basic Law states: "Die Würde des Menschen ist unantastbar" — "Human dignity shall be inviolable." This is the most important article in the entire constitution and is protected by the eternity clause (it can never be changed or removed). The right to life is in Article 2, freedom of religion in Article 4, and freedom of expression in Article 5.

questions.de: Was versteht man unter dem Recht der "Freizügigkeit" in Deutschland?
questions.en: What is meant by the right of "freedom of movement" in Germany?

opts.de: Man darf sich seinen Wohnort selbst aussuchen.
opts.en: You are allowed to choose your place of residence yourself.

opts.de: Man darf sich für eine andere Religion entscheiden.
opts.en: You are allowed to choose a different religion.

opts.de: Man darf sich in der Öffentlichkeit nur leicht bekleidet bewegen.
opts.en: You are allowed to move around in public only lightly clothed.

questions.exp_de: Das Recht der Freizügigkeit bedeutet, dass man seinen Wohnort in Deutschland frei wählen darf.
questions.exp_en: "Freizügigkeit" (freedom of movement, Article 11 of the Basic Law) means that German citizens have the right to freely choose where to live and work within Germany. This was historically significant because in the GDR (East Germany), citizens were not free to choose their residence or travel freely. The right to change professions is covered by Article 12 (freedom of occupation).

questions.de: Eine Partei in Deutschland verfolgt das Ziel, eine Diktatur zu errichten. Sie ist dann …
questions.en: A political party in Germany pursues the goal of establishing a dictatorship. It is then …

opts.en: oriented toward the rule of law.

questions.exp_de: Eine Partei, die eine Diktatur errichten will, verstößt gegen die freiheitlich-demokratische Grundordnung und ist damit verfassungswidrig.
questions.exp_en: Any party that aims to establish a dictatorship is unconstitutional (verfassungswidrig). The Basic Law protects Germany's democratic order, and Article 21 allows the Federal Constitutional Court to ban parties that seek to undermine or abolish the free democratic basic order. This provision exists because of Germany's experience with the Nazi party, which used democratic processes to destroy democracy itself.

questions.de: Welches ist das Wappen der Bundesrepublik Deutschland?
questions.en: Which is the coat of arms of the Federal Republic of Germany?
questions.exp_de: Das richtige Bild zeigt den einköpfigen Bundesadler auf goldenem Schild, das offizielle Wappen der Bundesrepublik Deutschland.
questions.exp_en: The coat of arms of Germany (Bundeswappen) features a black eagle with red beak and claws on a golden (yellow) shield. The eagle has been a symbol of German sovereignty for centuries, dating back to the Holy Roman Empire. The current design was adopted in 1950 for the Federal Republic of Germany.

questions.de: Was für eine Staatsform hat Deutschland?
questions.en: What form of government does Germany have?
questions.exp_de: Deutschland ist eine Republik.
questions.exp_en: Germany is a republic, meaning its head of state (the Federal President) is elected, not a hereditary monarch. Germany became a republic in 1918 when Kaiser Wilhelm II abdicated at the end of World War I. The Weimar Republic was followed by the Nazi dictatorship, and after WWII, the Federal Republic of Germany was established in 1949.

questions.de: In Deutschland sind die meisten Erwerbstätigen …
questions.en: In Germany, most employed people are …

opts.de: selbstständig mit einer eigenen Firma tätig.
bei einer Firma oder Behörde beschäftigt.
opts.en: employed by a company or government agency.

questions.exp_de: Die meisten Erwerbstätigen in Deutschland sind bei einer Firma oder Behörde angestellt, nicht selbstständig.
questions.exp_en: The vast majority of working people in Germany are employees (Arbeitnehmer) working for companies or government agencies. While small family businesses and self-employment exist, most people are in regular employment relationships with companies, institutions, or public authorities. Volunteering (Ehrenamt) is unpaid and not counted as employment.

questions.de: Wie viele Bundesländer hat die Bundesrepublik Deutschland?
questions.en: How many federal states does the Federal Republic of Germany have?
questions.exp_de: Die Bundesrepublik Deutschland hat 16 Bundesländer.
questions.exp_en: Germany consists of 16 federal states (Bundesländer): Baden-Württemberg, Bavaria, Berlin, Brandenburg, Bremen, Hamburg, Hesse, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Lower Saxony, North Rhine-Westphalia, Rhineland-Palatinate, Saarland, Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt, Schleswig-Holstein, and Thuringia. Three of these (Berlin, Hamburg, Bremen) are city-states (Stadtstaaten).

questions.de: Was ist kein Bundesland der Bundesrepublik Deutschland?
questions.en: Which is NOT a federal state of the Federal Republic of Germany?
questions.exp_de: Elsass-Lothringen ist kein deutsches Bundesland, sondern eine historische Region in Frankreich.
questions.exp_en: Alsace-Lorraine (Elsass-Lothringen) is not a German federal state — it is a region in France. It was part of Germany from 1871 to 1918 and again during the Nazi occupation (1940–1945), but has been French territory since the end of WWII. All the other options are legitimate German federal states.

questions.de: Deutschland ist …
questions.en: Germany is …

opts.en: a democratic and social federal state.
a social and socialist federal state.

questions.exp_de: Deutschland ist laut Grundgesetz ein demokratischer und sozialer Bundesstaat.
questions.exp_en: Article 20 of the Basic Law defines Germany as a "demokratischer und sozialer Bundesstaat" — a democratic and social federal state. This means Germany is democratic (power comes from the people), social (the state provides for those in need), and federal (power is shared between the central government and the 16 states). Germany is neither communist, monarchist, nor socialist.

questions.de: Deutschland ist …
questions.en: Germany is …
questions.exp_de: Deutschland ist ein Bundesstaat, bestehend aus 16 Bundesländern.
questions.exp_en: Germany is a federal state (Bundesstaat), meaning it is composed of several partially sovereign states (Bundesländer) that share power with the central government. The GDR (East Germany) was a socialist state, but unified Germany is not. Germany has not been a monarchy since 1918 and has not been a dictatorship since 1945.

questions.de: Wer wählt in Deutschland die Abgeordneten zum Bundestag?
questions.en: Who elects the members of the Bundestag in Germany?
questions.exp_de: Der Bundestag wird direkt vom wahlberechtigten Volk gewählt.
questions.exp_en: Members of the Bundestag (German parliament) are elected directly by the eligible voters (wahlberechtigtes Volk). Every German citizen aged 18 or older has the right to vote in federal elections. Elections are held every four years. The military, business sector, and government administration have no special role in electing parliament members.

questions.de: Welches Tier ist das Wappentier der Bundesrepublik Deutschland?
questions.en: Which animal is the heraldic animal of the Federal Republic of Germany?
questions.exp_de: Der Adler ist das Wappentier der Bundesrepublik Deutschland.
questions.exp_en: The eagle (Adler) is the heraldic animal of Germany, known as the "Bundesadler" (Federal Eagle). It has been a symbol of German authority since the Holy Roman Empire. The Berlin bear is the symbol of the city of Berlin, the lion appears on the coat of arms of several German states (like Bavaria and Hesse), and the horse is the symbol of Lower Saxony.

questions.de: Was ist kein Merkmal unserer Demokratie?
questions.en: What is NOT a feature of our democracy?
questions.exp_de: Pressezensur ist kein Merkmal unserer Demokratie — im Gegenteil, Deutschland garantiert Pressefreiheit.
questions.exp_en: Press censorship (Pressezensur) is NOT a feature of democracy — it is the opposite. In a democracy, the press must be free to report without government censorship. Regular elections, freedom of opinion, and multiple parties are all essential features of a functioning democracy. Press freedom is specifically protected by Article 5 of the Basic Law.

questions.de: Die Zusammenarbeit von Parteien zur Bildung einer Regierung nennt man in Deutschland …
questions.en: In Germany, the cooperation of parties to form a government is called a …
questions.exp_de: Die richtige Antwort ist: Koalition.
questions.exp_en: When two or more parties work together to form a government, this alliance is called a "Koalition" (coalition). Since no single party usually wins an absolute majority in German elections, coalitions are very common. The parties negotiate a coalition agreement (Koalitionsvertrag) that outlines their shared political goals. A "Fraktion" is a parliamentary group of one party, and a "Ministerium" is a government ministry.

questions.de: Was ist keine staatliche Gewalt in Deutschland?
questions.en: Which is NOT a branch of state power in Germany?
questions.exp_de: Die richtige Antwort ist: Presse
questions.exp_en: Germany has three branches of government (Gewaltenteilung): Legislative (Gesetzgebung — makes laws, e.g., Bundestag), Executive (Regierung — enforces laws, e.g., government/police), and Judiciary (Rechtsprechung — interprets laws, e.g., courts). The press is NOT a branch of state power. However, the media is sometimes informally called the "fourth estate" (vierte Gewalt) because of its important watchdog role.

questions.de: Welche Aussage ist richtig? In Deutschland …
questions.en: Which statement is correct? In Germany …

opts.de: sind Staat und Religionsgemeinschaften voneinander getrennt.
opts.en: the state and religious communities are separate from each other.

opts.de: ist der Staat abhängig von den Religionsgemeinschaften.
opts.en: the state is dependent on religious communities.

opts.de: bilden Staat und Religionsgemeinschaften eine Einheit.
opts.en: the state and religious communities form a single entity.

questions.exp_de: Die richtige Antwort ist: sind Staat und Religionsgemeinschaften voneinander getrennt.
questions.exp_en: Germany practices separation of church and state. While Germany is not as strictly secular as France (churches can collect taxes through the state, and religious education is offered in public schools), the state and religious communities are constitutionally separate. No religion has governmental authority, and the state does not favor any particular religion.

questions.de: Was ist Deutschland nicht?
questions.en: What is Germany NOT?
questions.exp_de: Die richtige Antwort ist: eine Monarchie
questions.exp_en: Germany is NOT a monarchy. It is a democracy, a constitutional state (Rechtsstaat), and a welfare state (Sozialstaat). Germany ended its monarchy in 1918 when Kaiser Wilhelm II abdicated at the end of World War I. Since then, Germany has been a republic with an elected head of state (the Federal President).

questions.de: Womit finanziert der deutsche Staat die Sozialversicherung?
questions.en: How does the German government finance social insurance?
questions.exp_de: Die richtige Antwort ist: Sozialabgaben
questions.exp_en: Social insurance in Germany is financed through social security contributions (Sozialabgaben), which are automatically deducted from employees' gross salaries. Both employers and employees contribute approximately equal shares. These contributions fund health insurance, pension insurance, unemployment insurance, long-term care insurance, and accident insurance. Church tax is a separate voluntary payment, and donations/membership fees play no role in public social insurance.

questions.de: Welche Maßnahme schafft in Deutschland soziale Sicherheit?
questions.en: Which measure provides social security in Germany?
questions.exp_de: Die richtige Antwort ist: die Krankenversicherung
questions.exp_en: Health insurance (Krankenversicherung) is part of the German social security system (Sozialversicherung). It is mandatory for all residents of Germany. Car insurance, property insurance, and liability insurance are private insurances that protect against specific risks but are not part of the social security system. Germany's social insurance has five pillars: health, pension, unemployment, long-term care, and accident insurance.

questions.de: Wie werden die Regierungschefinnen/Regierungschefs der meisten Bundesländer in Deutschland genannt?
questions.en: What are the heads of government of most German federal states called?
questions.exp_de: Die richtige Antwort ist: Ministerpräsidentin/Ministerpräsident
questions.exp_en: The heads of government in most German federal states are called "Ministerpräsident/in" (Minister-President). The exceptions are the three city-states: Berlin's head of government is the "Regierende/r Bürgermeister/in" (Governing Mayor), Hamburg's is the "Erste/r Bürgermeister/in" (First Mayor), and Bremen's is the "Präsident/in des Senats und Bürgermeister/in" (President of the Senate and Mayor).

questions.de: Die Bundesrepublik Deutschland ist ein demokratischer und sozialer …
questions.en: The Federal Republic of Germany is a democratic and social …
questions.exp_de: Die richtige Antwort ist: Bundesstaat.
questions.exp_en: As stated in Article 20 of the Basic Law, Germany is a "demokratischer und sozialer Bundesstaat" (democratic and social federal state). A Bundesstaat (federal state) is different from a Staatenbund (confederation — a loose alliance of independent states like the EU) and a Zentralstaat (centralized/unitary state like France). In a federal state, power is shared between a central government and regional governments.

questions.de: Was hat jedes deutsche Bundesland?
questions.en: What does every German federal state have?
questions.exp_de: Die richtige Antwort ist: eine eigene Regierung
questions.exp_en: Each German federal state has its own state government (Landesregierung), led by a Minister-President, with its own state parliament (Landtag) and state constitution. However, states do NOT have their own foreign ministers (foreign policy is a federal matter), their own currency (Germany uses the Euro throughout), or their own military (the Bundeswehr is the sole military force for all of Germany).

questions.de: Mit welchen Worten beginnt die deutsche Nationalhymne?
questions.en: With which words does the German national anthem begin?

opts.en: Joy, beautiful spark of the gods …

questions.exp_de: Die richtige Antwort ist: Einigkeit und Recht und Freiheit …
questions.exp_en: The German national anthem uses only the third verse of the "Deutschlandlied" (Song of Germany), written by August Heinrich Hoffmann von Fallersleben in 1841. It begins with "Einigkeit und Recht und Freiheit" (Unity and justice and freedom). "Freude schöner Götterfunken" is from Beethoven's "Ode to Joy" (the EU anthem). "Völker, hört die Signale" is from "The Internationale" (a socialist anthem). "Deutschland einig Vaterland" was from the GDR national anthem.

questions.de: Warum gibt es in einer Demokratie mehr als eine Partei?
questions.en: Why are there more than one party in a democracy?

opts.de: weil dadurch die unterschiedlichen Meinungen der Bürgerinnen und Bürger vertreten werden
opts.en: because this allows the diverse opinions of citizens to be represented

opts.de: damit Bestechung in der Politik begrenzt wird

questions.exp_en: Multiple parties exist in a democracy to represent the diversity of opinions and interests among citizens. questions.exp_en: New laws in Germany are enacted by parliament (the Bundestag, often with participation of the Bundesrat). While the government can propose laws, only parliament has the authority to pass them through a vote. Courts interpret and apply laws but do not create them. The police enforce laws but have no legislative power. This separation of powers is a fundamental principle of the Rechtsstaat.

A "Bürgerversammlung" (citizens' assembly) is NOT a constitutional organ — it is a concept from local or participatory democracy but not part of Germany's constitutional structure.

questions.exp_en: Educational policy in Germany is determined by the federal states (Bundesländer), not the central government. This is called "Kulturhoheit der Länder" (cultural sovereignty of the states). Each state has its own Ministry of Education and sets its own curriculum, school system, and educational standards. This is why school systems can differ significantly between states — for example, the number of years in primary school or the types of secondary schools available.

questions.exp_de: Die richtige Antwort ist: soziale Marktwirtschaft.
questions.exp_en: Germany's economic system is the "soziale Marktwirtschaft" (social market economy). This model was developed by Ludwig Erhard after WWII and combines free market principles with social welfare policies. Businesses operate freely and compete in the market, but the state intervenes to provide social security, prevent monopolies, and ensure fair working conditions. The GDR (East Germany) had a "Planwirtschaft" (planned economy), where the state controlled all economic activity.
